gaps.sentence: I'll lend you the tent ___ you bring it back dried.
gaps.explanation: 'Provided (that)' introduces the condition under which something will happen.

gaps.sentence: I wish you ___ so pessimistic about the project.
gaps.hint: a wish about a present attitude
gaps.explanation: Wishes about present states use 'were': were not.

gaps.sentence: If he had not left his passport at home, he ___ the earlier flight.
gaps.hint: third conditional result, would have participle
gaps.explanation: The unreal past result takes 'would have' plus the participle: would have caught.

gaps.sentence: If he ___ so stubborn, we would have reached an agreement by now.
gaps.hint: present cause with a result up to now
gaps.explanation: An unreal present cause can produce a result reaching into the past; formally 'were' is used: were not.

gaps.sentence: They would have won the match if their best player ___ injured.
gaps.hint: unreal past needs the past perfect
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition requires the past perfect: had not been.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ me tonight, I will send you the files first thing.
gaps.explanation: A realistic future condition uses the present simple after 'if': email.

gaps.sentence: You can borrow the car ___ you return it by Sunday.
gaps.explanation: 'Provided you return it' sets a condition.

gaps.sentence: I will tell her the news when I ___ her at the party.
gaps.hint: when clauses take present for future
gaps.explanation: Time clauses with future meaning use the present simple, not 'will': see.
